titleEn: Concrete and steel – or mangroves and forests? When it comes to climate adaptation, nature is much cheaper
titleZh: 混凝土与钢铁，还是红树林与森林？自然适应方案更经济
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: What’s the best way to protect ourselves against climate change? The default is to reach for concrete and steel to build seawalls, dykes, dams and drainage systems. These can work. But they are expensive and inflexible.
paragraphs.zh: 保护我们免受气候变化影响的最佳方法是什么？默认的方法是用混凝土和钢铁建造海堤、堤坝、水坝和排水系统。这些方法可以奏效，但它们昂贵且不灵活。

paragraphs.en: There’s another, much cheaper option which gets vastly less attention. Mangroves, forests and urban trees can help protect humans and their homes, farms and cities from floods, droughts, rising seas and heat.
paragraphs.zh: 还有另一种更便宜的选择，但却很少受到关注。红树林、森林和城市树木可以帮助保护人类及其家园、农场和城市免受洪水、干旱、海平面上升和高温的影响。

paragraphs.en: As our recent research shows, these methods aren’t fig leaves – they’re high-performance critical infrastructure.
paragraphs.zh: 正如我们最近的研究所示，这些方法不是遮羞布-它们是高性能的关键基础设施。

paragraphs.en: Unlike grey infrastructure of steel and concrete, these living systems can adapt as the climate shifts. Mangrove forests can shift as the sea rises, for example.
paragraphs.zh: 与灰色的钢筋混凝土基础设施不同，这些生命系统可以适应气候变化。例如，红树林可以随着海平面上升而变化。

paragraphs.en: Green infrastructure has proven itself cost-effective and functional in nations from Brazil to Kenya to Indonesia. But adoption could be much broader – if authorities properly considered nature as an infrastructure option.
paragraphs.zh: 从巴西到肯尼亚再到印度尼西亚，绿色基础设施已经证明了自己的成本效益和功能。但如果当局适当地将自然作为一种基础设施选择，那么采用的范围可能会更广。

paragraphs.en: The limits of concrete and steel
paragraphs.zh: 混凝土和钢筋的极限

paragraphs.en: Many engineered assets were designed for a stable climate that no longer exists.
paragraphs.zh: 许多工程资产是为不再存在的稳定气候而设计的。

paragraphs.en: Coastal defences designed to repel mid-20th century level storm surges are being breached with growing regularity.
paragraphs.zh: 旨在抵御世纪中期风暴潮的海岸防御系统正越来越经常地被破坏。

paragraphs.en: As rainfall patterns shift, a rise in extreme rainfall can overwhelm drainage systems built for the last century. In 2022, severe summer downpours caused the failure of water infrastructure in Jackson, Mississippi. This year, intense cloudbursts turned streets into raging rivers in Saitama, Japan.
paragraphs.zh: 随着降雨模式的转变，极端降雨量的增加可能会压垮上世纪建造的排水系统。2022年，夏季的倾盆大雨导致密西西比州杰克逊的供水基础设施瘫痪。今年，日本琦玉的强降雨将街道变成了汹涌的河流。

paragraphs.en: Once built, concrete and steel do their job until they fail. But living systems can respond by adjusting to new patterns of temperature, rainfall and sediment deposition rather than simply failing.
paragraphs.zh: 一旦建成，混凝土和钢筋就能发挥作用，直到它们失效。但生命系统可以通过适应新的温度、降雨和沉积物沉积模式来做出反应，而不是简单地失效。

paragraphs.en: The idea isn’t new. In the 1990s, New York City authorities spent roughly A$2.1 billion protecting forests and plants in the city’s watershed. As a result, they avoided the need to build a conventional filtration plant, which would have cost an estimated $8.6-11 billion.
paragraphs.zh: 这个想法并不新鲜。20世纪90年代，纽约市当局花费了大约21亿澳元保护该市流域的森林和植物。因此，他们避免了建造一座传统过滤厂的需要，这座工厂的成本估计为86亿至110亿美元。

paragraphs.en: Many other nations have embraced cheaper, more flexible green infrastructure.
paragraphs.zh: 许多其他国家已经接受了更便宜、更灵活的绿色基础设施。

paragraphs.en: Mangroves protect coastlines
paragraphs.zh: 红树林保护海岸线

paragraphs.en: Tropical nations face the worst risk from sea level rise, as they are home to more than 60% of the world’s low-lying coastlines.
paragraphs.zh: 热带国家面临海平面上升的最大风险，因为它们拥有世界上60%以上的低洼海岸线。

paragraphs.en: Even if greenhouse emissions are drastically reduced, by 2100 seas will rise about 0.6 metres above 2000 levels. If emissions don’t fall sharply, sea level rise will be more like 2.2m.
paragraphs.zh: 即使温室气体排放量大幅减少，到2100年，海平面将比2000年的水平高出0.6米，如果排放量不大幅减少，海平面将上升2.2米。

paragraphs.en: Without efforts to adapt, encroaching seas could do more than $27 trillion in damage globally.
paragraphs.zh: 如果不努力适应，侵蚀海洋可能会在全球造成超过27万亿美元的损失。

paragraphs.en: Governments often build seawalls and dykes to protect coasts. These can work, but they cost a great deal and can fail catastrophically under extreme conditions.
paragraphs.zh: 政府经常建造海堤和堤坝来保护海岸，这些措施可以奏效，但成本高昂，在极端条件下可能会发生灾难性的失败。

paragraphs.en: By contrast, fast-growing mangroves naturally dampen storm surges and inundation. Protection from the world’s existing mangrove forests is worth an estimated A$1.2 trillion over 100 years.
paragraphs.zh: 相比之下，快速生长的红树林可以自然地抑制风暴潮和洪水泛滥。据估计，保护世界上现有的红树林在100年内价值1.2万亿澳元。

paragraphs.en: Planting mangroves typically cost less than 50% of the cost of concrete and steel equivalents for the same protection, while the value of avoided property damage can be 10 to 100 times greater than planting costs.
paragraphs.zh: 种植红树林的成本通常不到同等保护的混凝土和钢材成本的50%，而避免财产损失的价值可能是种植成本的10至100倍。

paragraphs.en: In the Mekong Delta, authorities are combining grey and green infrastructure, planting mangrove belts to give built embankments a longer lifespan and cut maintenance costs.
paragraphs.zh: 在湄公河三角洲，当局正在结合灰色和绿色基础设施，种植红树林带，使建成的设施寿命更长，并降低维护成本。

paragraphs.en: Forests are water infrastructure
paragraphs.zh: 森林是水利基础设施

paragraphs.en: It makes good financial sense to replant forests in city watersheds, as they naturally filter rainwater as it fills dams. Protecting intact forests – and the watersheds they protect – is also sensible, as these act as vital water infrastructure, recycling water and even generating rainfall.
paragraphs.zh: 在城市流域重新种植森林在经济上很有意义，因为它们在雨水填充水坝时会自然过滤雨水。保护完整的森林--以及它们所保护的流域--也是明智的，因为它们是重要的水利基础设施，可以循环利用水，甚至产生降雨。

paragraphs.en: The rainfall and water recycling produced by the Brazilian Amazon rainforest is worth about $20 billion a year. This supports agriculture, power generation and regional water supplies.
paragraphs.zh: 巴西亚马逊雨林每年产生的降雨和水循环价值约200亿美元，支持农业、发电和区域供水。

paragraphs.en: Forests can even boost energy security in nations reliant on hydroelectricity, such as Brazil. When forests are cut down, rain washes more silt into rivers where it can fill up hydropower dams and reduces power generation.
paragraphs.zh: 森林甚至可以提高依赖水力发电的国家的能源安全，比如巴西。当森林被砍伐时，雨水会将更多的淤泥冲入河流，从而填满水电大坝，减少发电量。

paragraphs.en: Trees cool cities
paragraphs.zh: 树木为城市降温

paragraphs.en: Concrete, bricks and tarmac trap heat and make cities hotter than their surrounding areas. This urban heat island effect can pose a severe risk to health, particularly in rapidly urbanising parts of the Global South.
paragraphs.zh: 混凝土、砖块和柏油路面会吸收热量，使城市比周边地区更热。这种城市热岛效应可能对健康构成严重威胁，特别是在全球南部快速城市化的地区。

paragraphs.en: Street trees and urban forests can make cities significantly cooler, avoiding heat-related deaths and cutting energy demand.
paragraphs.zh: 街道树木和城市森林可以使城市显着凉爽，避免与热有关的死亡和减少能源需求。

paragraphs.en: Singapore’s plan to plant a million trees by 2030 is predicted to cut outdoor heat stress by 3–5°C and reduce the energy used for air-conditioning in summer by 6–9%.
paragraphs.zh: 新加坡计划到2030年种植100万棵树，预计将减少3 - 5 ° C的室外热应力，并减少6 - 9%的夏季空调能耗。

paragraphs.en: In Colombia, green corridors planted along roads and waterways have reduced average temperatures 2°C, returning $1.7 in avoided health costs for every $1 spent on the project.
paragraphs.zh: 在哥伦比亚，沿着道路和水道种植的绿色走廊使平均气温降低了2 ° C，在该项目上每花费1美元，就可以节省1.7美元的健康成本。

paragraphs.en: Unlocking green infrastructure
paragraphs.zh: 解锁绿色基础设施

paragraphs.en: The benefits of green infrastructure are well known. But investment in green infrastructure remains limited.
paragraphs.zh: 绿色基础设施的好处众所周知，但对绿色基础设施的投资仍然有限。

paragraphs.en: When governments want to build new infrastructure, their procurement rules typically favour traditional grey infrastructure, which come with established engineering standards and contractual certainty.
paragraphs.zh: 当政府想要建设新的基础设施时，它们的采购规则通常倾向于传统的灰色基础设施，这些基础设施具有既定的工程标准和合同确定性。

paragraphs.en: But these decisions often don’t weigh up green infrastructure fairly, because wider benefits such as avoided flood risks and water services aren’t typically included in the accounting framework used.
paragraphs.zh: 但这些决策往往没有公平地衡量绿色基础设施，因为避免洪水风险和供水服务等更广泛的好处通常不包括在所使用的会计框架中。

paragraphs.en: Four fixes
paragraphs.zh: 四个修正

paragraphs.en: To solve this problem, governments, climate adaptation funds and development banks will have to adopt four fixes:
paragraphs.zh: 为了解决这个问题，各国政府、气候适应基金和开发银行必须采取四项措施：

paragraphs.en: Recognise green infrastructure as a capital asset in national planning frameworks, governed by the same mechanisms as grey assets
paragraphs.zh: 将绿色基础设施视为国家规划框架中的资本资产，由与灰色资产相同的机制管理

paragraphs.en: Protect existing forests, mangroves and other green assets before new grey structures are built
paragraphs.zh: 在建造新的灰色结构之前，保护现有的森林、红树林和其他绿色资产

paragraphs.en: Ensure the value of ecosystems is included in project appraisals by switching to an accounting method which puts a value on intact ecosystems
paragraphs.zh: 确保将生态系统的价值纳入项目评估，改用对完整生态系统进行估值的会计方法

paragraphs.en: Ensure large development plans include both grey and green infrastructure designed for future climate scenarios.
paragraphs.zh: 确保大型发展计划包括为未来气候情景设计的灰色和绿色基础设施。

paragraphs.en: These shifts are technically feasible and economically justified.
paragraphs.zh: 这些转变在技术上是可行的，在经济上是合理的。

paragraphs.en: Politics and inertia are the biggest blockers. Grey infrastructure is the incumbent, while green infrastructure is the contender.
paragraphs.zh: 政治和惯性是最大的拦路虎，灰色基建是在位者，绿色基建是竞争者。

paragraphs.en: As damage from climate change intensifies, this will have to change. Green infrastructure is cheaper and more adaptable than grey. It’s not nice to have – it’s necessity.
paragraphs.zh: 随着气候变化造成的破坏加剧，这种情况必须改变。绿色基础设施比灰色基础设施更便宜，适应性更强。拥有并不好--这是必需品。
